teaching_point: Acne vulgaris: mixed comedones, inflammatory papules and pustules in a seborrhoeic (face) distribution — comedones are the hallmark lesion that separates acne from its mimics.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acne vulgaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-vulgaris

teaching_point: Comedonal acne: predominantly non-inflamed lesions — topical retinoid-based combination is the logical first choice; little role for antibiotics.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Comedonal acne (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/comedones

teaching_point: Open comedones (blackheads): dilated follicle with oxidised keratin/melanin plug — counsel that the dark colour is not dirt, so harsh scrubbing does not help.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Open comedones (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/comedones

teaching_point: Closed comedones (whiteheads): skin-coloured micro-papules best seen with side lighting/stretching — precursors of inflammatory lesions.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Closed comedones (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/comedones

teaching_point: Mild-to-moderate acne (NICE NG198 grouping): comedones with a few papules/pustules — 12-week topical fixed combination, no oral antibiotic.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mild acne (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-vulgaris

teaching_point: Moderate acne: more widespread inflammatory papules/pustules — still often topical first; consider topical + oral lymecycline/doxycycline per NG198 if moderate-to-severe.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Moderate acne (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-vulgaris

teaching_point: Severe acne with nodules and scarring risk — moderate-to-severe NG198 pathway; refer to consultant dermatologist if nodulocystic/scarring for isotretinoin assessment.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Severe acne (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-vulgaris

teaching_point: Nodulocystic acne on the face: deep painful nodules/cysts — high scarring risk; NG198 advises referral (isotretinoin is consultant-led).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nodulocystic acne: face (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/nodulocystic-acne

teaching_point: Acne conglobata pattern: chronic interconnecting nodules, abscesses, sinus tracts and grouped comedones without systemic illness — specialist referral; distinguish from acne fulminans.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nodulocystic acne (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/nodulocystic-acne

teaching_point: Truncal nodulocystic acne (chest): trunk involvement and scarring push towards specialist care; always examine back/chest.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nodulocystic acne: chest (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/nodulocystic-acne

teaching_point: Acne fulminans: sudden painful ulcerating/haemorrhagic crusted nodules, typically young males — may come with fever, arthralgia and bone pain: urgent same-day dermatology advice.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acne fulminans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-fulminans

teaching_point: Acne fulminans with ulceration and crusting — can be triggered by starting isotretinoin; managed with oral steroids ± cautious isotretinoin by specialists.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acne fulminans (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-fulminans

teaching_point: Acne fulminans in the context of SAPHO (synovitis–acne–pustulosis–hyperostosis–osteitis) — bone/joint pain with severe acne should prompt specialist review.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acne fulminans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sapho-syndrome

teaching_point: Isotretinoin cheilitis: near-universal dose-related lip dryness — counsel regular lip balm/emollient; useful marker of adherence.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cheilitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/isotretinoin

teaching_point: Early acne flare on isotretinoin — warn patients; a severe flare may represent isotretinoin-triggered acne fulminans (seek specialist advice).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acne flare (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/isotretinoin

teaching_point: Ice-pick atrophic acne scars — scarring at any severity is an NG198 referral trigger; prevent by treating early and effectively.
dermnet_caption: Ice pick scarring on the cheeks
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Ice pick scarring on the cheeks (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-scarring

teaching_point: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after acne in skin of colour — often the main concern; NG198 lists persistent pigmentary change as a referral consideration; daily sunscreen + azelaic acid/retinoid.
dermnet_caption: Post inflammatory pigmentation after facial acne in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Post inflammatory pigmentation after facial acne in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-scarring

teaching_point: Keloid scarring on the shoulders after acne in skin of colour — high-risk site/phenotype; treat inflammatory acne early and refer.
dermnet_caption: True keloids on the shoulders post acne in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — True keloids on the shoulders post acne in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-scarring

teaching_point: Adult (post-adolescent) acne: inflammatory papules favouring the lower face/jawline in women — ask about cycle, hirsutism, alopecia (PCOS screen).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Adult acne (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/adult-acne

teaching_point: Acne in polycystic ovary syndrome — look for hirsutism, irregular periods, acanthosis nigricans; combined oral contraceptive (UKMEC permitting) can help with topical therapy.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Polycystic ovarian syndrome (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/polycystic-ovary-syndrome

teaching_point: Hirsutism in PCOS — a clinical sign of hyperandrogenism to check whenever adult female acne is persistent or treatment-resistant.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hirsutism (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/polycystic-ovary-syndrome

teaching_point: Acne in pregnancy: avoid topical and oral retinoids and tetracyclines; options usually topical benzoyl peroxide/azelaic acid ± erythromycin if needed (check current guidance).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acne in pregnancy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acne-in-pregnancy

teaching_point: Acanthosis nigricans on the neck: velvety grey-brown thickening with accentuated skin markings — commonest association is obesity/insulin resistance; not "dirt".
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acanthosis nigricans on the neck (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acanthosis-nigricans

teaching_point: Axillary acanthosis nigricans — screen HbA1c/fasting glucose, lipids, BP; ask about PCOS symptoms; weight management is the core treatment.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Axillary acanthosis nigricans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acanthosis-nigricans

teaching_point: Acanthosis nigricans close-up — red flags for malignant AN: sudden/rapid extensive onset in a slim older adult, mucosal or palmar involvement ("tripe palms"), weight loss → urgent investigation.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acanthosis nigricans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acanthosis-nigricans

teaching_point: Papulopustular rosacea on the cheeks: papules/pustules on background erythema with NO comedones; flushing triggers — key point vs acne.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papulopustular rosacea on the cheeks (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: Erythematotelangiectatic + papulopustular rosacea — central convex face; topical ivermectin/azelaic acid/metronidazole, oral doxycycline 40 mg MR for moderate–severe.
dermnet_caption: Erythematotelangiectatic and papulopustular rosacea on the cheeks
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythematotelangiectatic and papulopustular rosacea on the cheeks (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: Rhinophyma (phymatous rosacea) — not a feature of acne; refer for physical treatments if distressing.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Rhinophyma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: Papulopustular plus ocular rosacea — ask about gritty eyes/blepharitis; eye pain, photophobia or reduced vision needs same-day ophthalmology.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papulopustular and ocular rosacea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: Pyoderma faciale (rosacea fulminans): abrupt confluent nodules/pustules on the central face in a young woman, no comedones, often stress-related — urgent dermatology referral.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pyoderma faciale, rosacea fulminans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pyoderma-faciale

teaching_point: Rosacea fulminans: draining nodules and sinus formation on a red base — treated by specialists (oral steroid then isotretinoin), unlike ordinary acne.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pyoderma faciale, rosacea fulminans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pyoderma-faciale

teaching_point: Steroid-induced acneiform eruption: monomorphic papulopustules on chest/upper trunk with few or no comedones — ask about oral/topical/inhaled steroids, anabolic steroids, other drugs.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Steroid-induced acne vulgaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/steroid-acne

teaching_point: Topical steroid-induced papulopustular rosacea on the face — stop facial steroid (may flare first); never treat facial papules with potent steroid.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Steroid induced papulopustular rosacea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: Florid perioral dermatitis from potent topical steroid — perioral papules with a clear rim at the lip; stop steroid, use topical metronidazole/azelaic or oral tetracycline.
dermnet_caption: Florid perioral dermatitis due to potent topical steroid use
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Florid perioral dermatitis due to potent topical steroid use (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/periorificial-dermatitis

teaching_point: Gram-negative folliculitis: sudden pustular flare around nose/chin in someone on long-term tetracycline for acne — swab pustules (and nares); stop the tetracycline; specialist may use isotretinoin.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Gram-negative folliculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/gram-negative-folliculitis

teaching_point: Malassezia (pityrosporum) folliculitis: itchy, uniform small papules/pustules on upper trunk — heat, sweat, occlusion, recent antibiotics; no comedones.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Malassezia folliculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/malassezia-folliculitis

teaching_point: Malassezia folliculitis close-up: monomorphic follicular papules — responds to ketoconazole shampoo as a wash or topical azoles; oral itraconazole/fluconazole if extensive (check interactions).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Malassezia folliculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/malassezia-folliculitis

teaching_point: Pseudomonas (hot-tub) folliculitis: follicular papulopustules under swimwear areas 1–2 days after a spa/hot tub — usually self-limiting; check the pool chlorination.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pseudomonas folliculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/spa-pool-folliculitis

teaching_point: Spa pool folliculitis on the trunk — history of exposure is the key clue; antibiotics (e.g. ciprofloxacin) only if severe or persistent.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Spa pool folliculitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/spa-pool-folliculitis

teaching_point: Superficial staphylococcal folliculitis — pustules centred on hair follicles, often after shaving/occlusion; a common acne look-alike on beard area and buttocks.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Superficial bacterial folliculitis (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/folliculitis
